reviewContext.userProblem: Issue #184 asked that every routed riela subcommand print usage and exit 0 for --help/-h. The first fix landed at dd6c94c9. The audit of main @ 0f18d867 (design §6) found the runtime correct but two gaps: delegated runners (gc, session prune, session reconcile, cache, environment) have only partial end-to-end help regression coverage (GC1), and the uniform help rule is not mentioned in any user-facing doc (GC2).
requiredOutcomes: GC1: SubcommandHelpApplicationTests.testTopLevelAndDelegatedHelpStayUnchanged covers 11 delegated argument lists (gc, session prune, session reconcile, cache put, environment status with --help and -h, plus environment reload --help), each asserting exit .success, non-empty stdout, no helpRequested, and no {"error" prefix.

GC2/D5: README.md gets one short paragraph under ## Control Surfaces after the SurfaceCatalog paragraph, stating the uniform --help/-h rule, the -- terminator rule, the --option=--help literal form, and that riela gateway <name> --help shows the gateway's own help.

GC3: the focused filter swift test --filter 'SubcommandHelp|StorageHelpBackstopTests|CommandParsingTests|WorkflowRunHelpTests|PasskeyCommandTests' passes with >0 tests and 0 failures, and storage compact --help/-h, session status --help, workflow validate --help print usage and exit 0 from .build/debug/riela.
nonGoals: No change under Sources/; rielaCLIHelpText unchanged (D5).
No change to VERSION or Package.swift (already 0.2.83).
No usage lines for kaiba, routine or version (D2); they keep the full top-level help.

constraints: Run swift build/test/swiftlint via arch -arm64 /bin/zsh -lc from the repository root, in the foreground, with the focused filter; the full suite is optional.
SwiftPM .build is a pre-existing gitignored cache; writing it is authorized and is not a tracked write.
Evidence and logs go only under tmp/issue-184-gap/<planId-or-chg-dir>/ and are never committed.
Workers share one working tree: no git commit/stash/checkout/branch; read files fresh and record before/after SHA-256.
designDecisionsAndRationale: D1: one detector (CLIHelpRequest.detect) in RielaCLIApplication.runParsed; per-parser help is not added.
D3: a help token before -- always wins; literal values use --opt=--help. This is why README states the --option=--help form.
D4: delegated runners keep their own ArgumentParser USAGE help; tests therefore assert exit code and non-empty stdout, not exact text.
D5: the help rule is documented in README.md only, so top-level help output and §2.3 usage slices stay unchanged.
intentionalTradeoffs: Delegated-runner tests do not assert exact help text or empty stderr, since ArgumentParser output is not part of the contract.
chg-01 runs a whole-package swift build while chg-02 edits only README.md in the same wave; README cannot affect the build (reviewer low finding).
If a delegated case fails end to end, chg-01 records a finding without touching Sources/; reconcile decides a serial follow-up.
supportedEdgeCases: Both --help and -h for every delegated runner.
environment reload --help returns help before any reload or network work.
Required-argument commands (session status, workflow validate) print usage without the argument.
Tokens after -- and --option=--help are never treated as help requests.
outOfScopeEdgeCases: Running serve or auth invite help end to end (covered by detector-only SubcommandHelpTests.testSurfaceAudit).
Command-specific usage for kaiba, routine and version.
Cross-module RielaCLITests regressions outside the focused filter (full-module run optional at integration).
residualRisks: StorageCompactCommandTests failures predate #184 and are excluded from the filter (not regressions).
No live build or test evidence exists at plan time; covered by chg-01 verification and the integration binary checks.
chg-01 Verification 4 git diff --stat will not list the untracked progress log; use git status for that evidence (reviewer low finding).
